Have your say on our draft Equity in the Arts Policy – Te Ara Mana Tautika o ngā Toi

We’re inviting artists, ringatoi, organisations and communities to share feedback on the draft Te Ara Mana Tautika o ngā Toi – Equity in the Arts Policy. 

This draft sets out how Creative New Zealand will support equity (fairness) in the arts and ngā toi Māori and deliver to our statutory purpose ‘to encourage, promote and support the arts in New Zealand for the benefit of all New Zealanders’. 

We need your whakaaro to help shape the final version of the policy and ensure it reflects the realities and aspirations of artists and communities across Aotearoa New Zealand. 

Read more: https://creativenz.govt.nz/equityinthearts

Queen's Cash Competition

To celebrate and support the businesses that make our CBD special, we’re running a Shop & Win competition in collaboration with The Breeze.

Every time you shop at a participating business you’ll go in the draw to win the Queen's Cash - $1,000 to spend in town.

The winner can spend their Queen's Cash across as many participating businesses as they want.

Kaitiaki Whenua - Trainee Ranger Programme: Wāhi Tapu & Kaitiakitanga

Join Rāwiri Taylor to explore two Trainee Ranger programme electives - Wāhi Tapu and Kaitiakitanga - and build cultural confidence for conservation mahi. Learn the significance of wāhi tapu and taonga tūturu, the tikanga (including tapu and noa) that guides safe, respectful practice, and how to engage with iwi and hapū. You’ll also deepen your understanding of kaitiakitanga (guardianship): the responsibilities of a kaitiaki and how to apply Māori values and mātauranga within Te Ao Māori to environmental stewardship.

Kaitiaki Whenua - Trainee Ranger Programme: Foliar Browse Index Elective

Join tutor Becs Gibson in a native lowland tōtara forest as she introduces the Foliar Browse Index elective. You’ll learn a quick, practical way to assess canopy health - spotting browse, dieback, and other signs of pest activity - so you can see whether pest control is working and respond early when it’s not. This elective is ideal for those interested in ecological monitoring and pest management and offers a hands-on taste of real conservation mahi and a useful monitoring skill for the workplace.

Kaitiaki Whenua - Trainee Ranger Programme: Practical Conservation Operations Elective

Discover how the Kaitiaki Training Ranger programme empowers students with hands-on skills and confidence in river crossing, helicopter safety, and four-wheel drive training in this elective. Join Fay McKenzie as she shares how practical experience builds confidence and prepares future conservation professionals for real-world challenges.

Tutors: Fay McKenzie, Geoff Button, external helicopter providers

Get ready for an immersive experience in the field! This course equips you with essential skills for working safely and effectively in remote conservation environments. You’ll learn how to:
• Safely operate around helicopters
• Drive a 4WD vehicle on rugged terrain
• Read and cross rivers confidently, both solo and in groups

With a mix of theory and hands-on training, including online modules and supervised practical sessions, this course prepares you for the realities of conservation work in Aotearoa’s wild landscapes.

Please note that a Learner driver's licence is needed, and at least a restricted licence is expected. Practical experience driving a manual vehicle is also required.

Join Fay McKenzie and the team to gain practical skills in river crossing, helicopter safety, and four-wheel drive training, all essential for remote conservation work. This course blends theory and hands-on sessions, building your confidence for field challenges. A minimum of a restricted license and manual driving experience is required.

Kaitiaki Whenua - Trainee Ranger Programme: Recreational Maintenance Elective

Ever wondered how DOC keeps tracks and huts in top shape? This course introduces you to the fundamentals of recreational maintenance. Join Geoff Button to learn how DOC plans, builds, and maintains tracks, huts, and park amenities. You’ll cover visitor needs, safe track upkeep (including scrub bars and vegetation clearance), and how to report issues so they’re picked up in work plans - helping protect visitors and care for the whenua.

Discover the Kaitiaki Whenua - Trainee Ranger programme.

Discover how the Trainee Ranger programme has been empowering conservation professionals for over 25 years, blending practical skills, plant identification, and Māori environmental principles to create confident rangers dedicated to protecting New Zealand’s natural treasures.

Tū i te ora Scholarship - Northland

Northland Regional Council’s Tū i te ora Scholarship recognises and supports students to undertake study, research or training that relates to council’s environmental and regulatory functions including; Te Tiriti Partnerships & Engagement, Climate Action, Biodiversity & Science and Rivers and Natural Hazards/Civil Defence. Our programme is a springboard for future environmental leaders and champions, whilst contributing to council’s vision ‘Tiakina te taiao, tuia te here tangata - Nurture the environment, bring together the people’

Read more and apply here: https://www.nrc.govt.nz/scholarship

Ohura Township Flooding Sunday 19 April 2026

Flooding swept through Ohura township in the early hours of Sunday morning 19 April 2026 requiring some whanau to escape to safety through chest high water. 

The next day the NZDF flew Ruapehu Mayor Weston Kirton, Emergency Management Minister Mark Mitchell, and elected representatives and staff from Horizons Regional Council over the flooded river catchment before landing in the township to meet with impacted residents.

This video shows the flooding in Ohura township from the air.

Emergency Management Minister Mark Mitchell in Ohura Sunday 19 April 2026

ASB Good as Gold: Erina 'Edz' Wehi-Barton

This week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient is Erina “Edz” Wehi‑Barton of Te Kūiti, a tireless community leader whose generosity and drive strengthen the whole town. 

Edz is the President of the local Waka Ama Club, leading more than 80 members and creating opportunities for tamariki to compete at a national level while promoting health, wellbeing, environmental care, and Te Reo Māori. When resources are scarce, Edz steps in. She maintains and repairs the waka and equipment, often teaching herself and others new skills to keep the club running. 

Beyond sport, Edz is a constant presence across the community, thought of as the Marae "Mrs Fix It", running educational seminars, supporting whānau, driving buses, and repairing essential services. Studying toward a PhD while working and training, Edz’s impact is defined by aroha, mahi, and unwavering service. ASB is proud to recognise Edz with $10,000 as this week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient.

ASB Good as Gold: Mike Taylor

This week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient is Mike Taylor of Riversdale. 

Mike has given more than 20 years of service to Surf Life Saving at Riversdale Beach as a lifeguard, trainer, examiner and long‑standing Club Captain. Under Mike’s leadership, the Riversdale Beach Surf Life Saving Club has achieved national success while remaining a welcoming hub for young lifeguards. 

Mike is also a trusted first responder whose commitment has helped keep a remote coastal community safe for decades. Often first on the scene for medical emergencies, Mike is effectively on call 24/7, providing critical care while ambulances or helicopters travel long distances to reach Riversdale. Over the years, his calm, dependable presence has made a life changing difference for countless locals and visitors. A farmer, long‑serving Rural Fire Force volunteer, and many other roles, Mike’s contribution is defined by humility, service and an unwavering dedication to others. ASB is thrilled to recognise Mike with $10,000 as this week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient.

Kaitiaki Whenua - Trainee Ranger Programme: Wāhi Tapu & Kaitiakitanga

Join Rāwiri Taylor to explore two Trainee Ranger programme electives - Wāhi Tapu and Kaitiakitanga - and build cultural confidence for conservation mahi. Learn the significance of wāhi tapu and taonga tūturu, the tikanga (including tapu and noa) that guides safe, respectful practice, and how to engage with iwi and hapū. You’ll also deepen your understanding of kaitiakitanga (guardianship): the responsibilities of a kaitiaki and how to apply Māori values and mātauranga within Te Ao Māori to environmental stewardship.

Kaitiaki Whenua - Trainee Ranger Programme: Foliar Browse Index Elective

Join tutor Becs Gibson in a native lowland tōtara forest as she introduces the Foliar Browse Index elective. You’ll learn a quick, practical way to assess canopy health - spotting browse, dieback, and other signs of pest activity - so you can see whether pest control is working and respond early when it’s not. This elective is ideal for those interested in ecological monitoring and pest management and offers a hands-on taste of real conservation mahi and a useful monitoring skill for the workplace.

Kaitiaki Whenua - Trainee Ranger Programme: Practical Conservation Operations Elective

Discover how the Kaitiaki Training Ranger programme empowers students with hands-on skills and confidence in river crossing, helicopter safety, and four-wheel drive training in this elective. Join Fay McKenzie as she shares how practical experience builds confidence and prepares future conservation professionals for real-world challenges.

Tutors: Fay McKenzie, Geoff Button, external helicopter providers

Get ready for an immersive experience in the field! This course equips you with essential skills for working safely and effectively in remote conservation environments. You’ll learn how to:
• Safely operate around helicopters
• Drive a 4WD vehicle on rugged terrain
• Read and cross rivers confidently, both solo and in groups

With a mix of theory and hands-on training, including online modules and supervised practical sessions, this course prepares you for the realities of conservation work in Aotearoa’s wild landscapes.

Please note that a Learner driver's licence is needed, and at least a restricted licence is expected. Practical experience driving a manual vehicle is also required.

Join Fay McKenzie and the team to gain practical skills in river crossing, helicopter safety, and four-wheel drive training, all essential for remote conservation work. This course blends theory and hands-on sessions, building your confidence for field challenges. A minimum of a restricted license and manual driving experience is required.

Kaitiaki Whenua - Trainee Ranger Programme: Recreational Maintenance Elective

Ever wondered how DOC keeps tracks and huts in top shape? This course introduces you to the fundamentals of recreational maintenance. Join Geoff Button to learn how DOC plans, builds, and maintains tracks, huts, and park amenities. You’ll cover visitor needs, safe track upkeep (including scrub bars and vegetation clearance), and how to report issues so they’re picked up in work plans - helping protect visitors and care for the whenua.

Discover the Kaitiaki Whenua - Trainee Ranger programme.

Discover how the Trainee Ranger programme has been empowering conservation professionals for over 25 years, blending practical skills, plant identification, and Māori environmental principles to create confident rangers dedicated to protecting New Zealand’s natural treasures.

How to decontaminate tools safely – Asbestos safety

After working with asbestos, your tools and equipment need to be decontaminated before your respirator and PPE. This is to stop harmful fibres spreading outside the asbestos work area.

Disposing of asbestos-related waste, respirators, and PPE safely – Asbestos safety

People working with asbestos and asbestos waste must make sure contaminated materials are disposed of safely.

How to wear a disposable respirator safely – Asbestos safety

You cannot see asbestos fibres, but if you breathe any in it can damage your lungs and lead to early death. Wearing a respirator that seals to your face will help protect you. This involves two steps: having a fit test done by a competent person, and checking your respirator still seals well every time.

Taking off your respirator and PPE safely – Asbestos safety

You cannot see asbestos fibres, but if you breath any in it can damage your lungs and lead to early death. Taking off your respirator and PPE safely stops the spread of dangerous fibres that can harm you and other people.

How to wear a reusable respirator safely – Asbestos safety

You cannot see asbestos fibres, but if you breathe any in it can damage your lungs and lead to early death. Wearing a respirator that seals to your face will help protect you.
